areas.name: PS2 Route and Preserved Online Play
areas.location_cue: The PS2 title screen, memory-card setup, Scenario Select, Network Play, and an OBSRV lobby.
areas.note: Use a clean selected route; the revival server supplements rather than replaces offline completion.

levels.1: The complete offline route belongs to one platform release.
levels.2: Play an original PS2 disc on native hardware or a tested PS2 emulator.
levels.3: Confirm the disc region, memory-card identity, video mode, controller, real-time status screen, and scenario save behavior before starting. No remaster or secondary platform adds completion content.

items.label: Start with a Fresh Memory Card

levels.1: Imported completion data can silently unlock the collection.
levels.2: Use a clean card for the measured unlock route and clone it after every scenario tier.
levels.3: Create a blank card, boot the chosen build, and verify that only the intended starting scenario and collection entries are present. Keep one untouched baseline plus rotating offline, online, SP-item, and reward backups.

levels.1: Current archival multiplayer uses the Japanese network-enabled build.
levels.2: Use a lawfully owned Japanese Biohazard Outbreak disc with the current OBSRV connection route.
levels.3: As of 2026-07-14, OBSRV accepts the Japanese editions. Dump your own disc and BIOS, use native PS2 networking or a current PCSX2 network build, create a fresh connection profile, and apply an optional translation patch only after preserving the clean image.

levels.1: The official service is closed, but a revival server preserves cooperative play.
levels.2: Register separately, configure the documented DNS or automatic connection, and enter Network Play.
levels.3: Follow OBSRV’s current setup page, enter its live network values rather than hard-coding an old address, authenticate with your own account, and reach a lobby. Do not use a shared pre-completed card when measuring unlock progress.

levels.1: The cooperative design includes actions absent from an ordinary solo run.
levels.2: Create a private room and clear one scenario with four human players.
levels.3: Agree on a spoiler-safe route beforehand, assign key-item and recovery roles, use only in-game calls, trade at least one item, assist an injured partner, and finish with all four connected. Repeat if a disconnect replaces completion evidence.

levels.1: Online defeat can briefly change the player’s role instead of ending immediately.
levels.2: On a cloned session, allow one player’s virus gauge to fill while teammates remain active.
levels.3: Use a private consenting group, remove valuable items first, let the selected gauge reach 100%, and record the temporary player-controlled hostile state until it ends. Restore the clean card afterward; this is an archival feature test, not a normal clear strategy.

levels.1: Not every regional disc shipped with the same online feature.
levels.2: Document that the PAL release lacks the original network-play route.
levels.3: Boot a lawful PAL copy only for version comparison, capture its main-menu options, and keep it outside the selected completion save. Use the Japanese build for preserved online play and the chosen original build for offline completion.

levels.1: Learn the physical route first; later runs can target checklist branches.

levels.1: The final menu entry appears after the initial set is cleared.
levels.2: Complete the other four scenarios on any available difficulty.

levels.1: A full first pass enables a harder shared ruleset.
levels.2: Clear all five scenarios on Easy or Normal, then purchase Hard Mode for 2,000 points.
levels.3: Complete all five scenario records, open Collection > Extra, buy Hard Mode, and clear each scenario on Hard without Infinity. Save after every clear because the set gates both Very Hard and Lone Wolf.

levels.1: The highest standard difficulty requires the full Hard set.
levels.2: Clear all five scenarios on Hard, then purchase Very Hard for 3,000 points.
levels.3: Verify every Hard completion mark, buy Very Hard from Collection > Extra, and clear all five scenarios on it with ordinary resources. Use separate scenario backups because items, enemies, and SP paths differ.

levels.1: A completed Hard set also enables partner-free offline play.
levels.2: Clear all five scenarios on Hard, buy Lone Wolf for 10,000 points, and finish every scenario alone.
levels.3: Purchase Lone Wolf after the Hard set, enable it before character selection, confirm no AI partners spawn, and clear each scenario once. Use character abilities and route-specific caches to compensate for missing partner inventory.

levels.1: The event checklist, not a difficulty clear, gates unlimited resources.
levels.2: Reach 100% on all five event checklists, then purchase Infinity Mode for 50,000 points.
levels.3: Accumulate every checklist event across repeat runs, confirm each scenario displays 100%, buy Infinity, and start a test scenario. Fire every firearm and use several durability-based melee weapons to verify neither ammunition nor durability decreases.

levels.1: Scenario and character pools together form the complete hidden-object archive.

levels.1: Checklist progress accumulates across mutually exclusive runs.
levels.2: Bring all five scenario event percentages to 100%.

levels.1: Files count both as clues and as checklist events.
